repo:objectstack#4 · os-elon-musk · session_016WV4d1H9ixhgepGZ7fawhL

**L1 verdict (L1-a): CHANGES** at head `73a678ade557bddda28305ca0e446ccb33e413bf`. There are two small text fixes in the ADR-0013 addendum. Everything else checks out. I am posting this before CI finishes because both fixes need a new head anyway.

**Checked and correct:**
- **Install model.** Point 1 states ruling `7023437637` ① faithfully: hosted is one ObjectOS app, and self-hosted means each organization brings its own app. The mapping onto §9's two shapes (L511) is right.
- **Tier.** The tier paragraph matches ruling `7023709522` clause for clause. Open: a self-hosted organization's own app, one `sys_channel_account` row per organization, and the confirm-once `sys_channel_user_link` binding. Enterprise: the hosted one-click app, managed credentials and vault, account health, and the managed multi-workspace lifecycle (ADR-0022 §4, ADR-0143).
- **Person binding.** Point 2 matches ②: a link is proposed by email match and confirmed once by the person. `sys_channel_user_link` is the person link and `sys_channel_account` the organization install. Replacing §8 item 2's "auto-create the link row" (L479) is a correct consequence of the ruling.
- **Scope.** The addendum is scoped to outbound per-person delivery under ADR-0030 and ADR-0022. The status line and the addendum's own header both say only the addendum is accepted and the rest stays Draft. Who may remove a link is listed as open.
- **ADR-0030.** The amendment strikes "enterprise-tier" and adds one dated status-line entry. That follows that record's own amendment convention, and the wording matches `7023709522`.
- **README.** The README row is generated: `adr-index --report` reports it current.

**Changes needed:**
1. **Point 3 brings in Draft §3.** It says DMs are "opened with §3's new-DM session key (`slack:ACC:dm:USER`, no thread segment)". The addendum's own Scope paragraph puts "sessions and threads" out of scope and keeps them Draft. §3 (`sessionKey` grammar) is a Draft section, so citing its key format in accepted text accepts part of it by implication. That contradicts the header line "nothing above it is accepted by implication". Neither ruling says anything about session keys. **Fix:** drop the session-key clause and keep "Direct messages to the linked person only."
2. **"Risk 4 stands as written" misquotes Risk 4.** Risk 4 as written says: "refuse the auto-link **and send a clarifying DM**". The addendum paraphrases it as "an ambiguous email proposes nothing". A clarifying DM to a Slack user who has no confirmed link conflicts with point 2's "a proposal nobody confirmed delivers nothing". **Fix:** state the outcome alone, for example "An email that matches more than one user proposes nothing (Risk 4's refusal; its clarifying DM is out of this scope)", or simply drop the cross-reference.

Both fixes are one-line deletions or rewordings, with no new rulings needed. After the fix I will re-check the delta on the new head once it is green.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `dba349aa1de38ce18b9a85233940ae357936dcb5`
Local-runs: none
Scope: docs/adr/0013-bidirectional-messaging.md, docs/adr/0030-notification-platform-convergence.md, docs/adr/README.md + none
Security-touching: yes

Read for this record: card #34730 (body and all nine comments), PR #35670 (body, file list, net diff of the head against `main`, merge base `5dd856f4`), the check-runs on the head. Code and ADRs outside the diff were read on `main`, never reviewed. `Security-touching: yes` because the addendum hunk teaches person binding, who may remove a link, where an install's token sits by tier, and the permission step 2 must name.

### ① Derived judgments

- The diff is three files under `docs/adr/`, +71 / -4, no implementing code: `+ none` holds.
- Ruling `7023437637` (three points) is stated faithfully. Install model: hosted one ObjectOS app, self-hosted own app per organization. Binding: an email match proposes, the person confirms once, an unconfirmed proposal delivers nothing, and §8 item 2's auto-create is replaced for this scope; `sys_channel_user_link` is the person, `sys_channel_account` the install. Destination: DMs only, channel posting stays on `connector_action` (ADR-0022 §2). No DMs-only leak found: §9's `chat:write.public` and channel scopes stay Draft and the addendum accepts nothing above it.
- Ruling `7023709522` (open tier) is stated without widening in ADR-0013: open = the self-hosted own-app install with a supplied token, one row per organization, plus the confirm-once link; enterprise keeps the hosted one-click app, managed credentials and the vault, account health and the managed multi-workspace lifecycle. All four enterprise items are present.
- Rider of `7023586880` (state the tier of the self-hosted install) is met by the Tier paragraph of point 1.
- Ruling `7024100939`: the authority (the person and an organization administrator) is stated. All five riders are present under "Step 2 owes"; two are paraphrased with loss, see S3.
- The "What `main` holds" paragraph checks out on `main`: no `sys_channel_account` outside `docs/adr/`, `sys_channel_user_link` only in `docs/handoff/adr-0030-notification-convergence.md`, `service-messaging` registers inbox, email, sms and push, and `connector-slack` is composed only by `examples/app-showcase`.
- README row for ADR-0013 reads "Draft — 2026-05-26 · Amended (2026-11-19, rulings ..." and matches the status line; the ADR stays Draft with an accepted addendum. The `Lint · docs & code guards` check-run on this head is green.
- Check-runs on the head: every run that executed concluded success; the rest are skipped. None failed.

### ② Semver level

None. Nothing under any package's `files[]` changes; a `docs/adr/` diff publishes nothing. The PR carries `skip-changeset`, `Check Changeset` is skipped on the head, and `Clause-②: no` is correct. No changeset is owed.

### ③ Boundary flags

- The dev report's one open question (who may remove a person link) was ruled by `7024100939` after the report, and this head records it. Answered.
- The addendum lists no question as open. One point the card raised is not ruled and not marked: a manual connect for a person whose emails do not match (card ask 1, "manual OAuth connect"). See S4.
- No dev flag, no SQL, no id materialisation in the diff.
- PR body is behind the head, see S5.

### ④ Design judgment

S1 (should-fix) — ADR-0022 §4 is left reading against the addendum. Its ADR-0143 amendment note (Accepted) says "the `sys_channel_account` lifecycle of a messaging channel" keeps the enterprise placement, with no "multi-tenant" qualifier, and comment `7023586880` itself read that note as placing the self-hosted own-app install on the enterprise side. Ruling `7023709522` then put that install in the open tier. The addendum reconciles inside ADR-0013 only (it reads the row as the managed multi-workspace lifecycle); ADR-0022 gets no dated note or pointer, so a reader of the Accepted record still finds the old line. Add one dated amendment note under ADR-0022 §4 pointing at the addendum, as was done for ADR-0030.

S2 (should-fix) — the seam list does not reach the first consumer. On `main`, `emit` defaults to `['inbox']` when a producer names no channels (`messaging-service.ts`), and plugin-approvals requests exactly `['inbox', 'email']` (`APPROVAL_EMAIL_CHANNELS`, `approval-service.ts`). Preferences filter requested channels; they never add one. A registered `slack` channel therefore receives no approval notice, and the card's acceptance ("an approval request reaches the bound person by DM") fails with every listed seam built. Name the missing seam: who requests the `slack` channel (the producers' channel lists, or fan-out). Related: `MessagingChannel.isAvailable` answers per organization only, so "no confirmed link" needs a per-recipient skip that is not a dead-lettered delivery; name it as owed, not designed.

S3 (should-fix) — two riders of `7024100939` are narrowed. Rider 3 says removal on "ban or loss of org membership"; the addendum says the user "leaves the organization", which does not cover a member removed by an administrator, the offboarding case the ruling was for. It also drops "automatically" and the `deleteBehavior: 'cascade'` form (as `sys_user_device`). Rider 2 says the person is told "by inbox/email"; the addendum says only "a notice". Restore the ruled wording.

S4 (should-fix) — two sentences in point 2 and the seam list go beyond the ruling. "An email that matches more than one user proposes nothing" is in no ruling; it is the seat's derivation from Draft §8 item 2 and Risk 4, and `sys_user.email` is globally unique on `main`, so it can only mean the Slack side. Mark it as derived or move it to step 2. "Connect and disconnect on the person's notification settings page" can be read as a manual connect without an email match, which is not ruled; say that connect is the confirmation of a proposal, and that the no-match case is not decided.

S5 (should-fix) — the PR body describes head `73a678ad`: it cites two rulings, says "Who may remove a link is listed as **open**", counts +68 / -4, and its gate evidence is for that head. The head now records `7024100939`. The maintainer merges ADRs by hand from this body; bring it to the head.

N1 (nit) — point 1 cites "(§4)" for the install row. §4's schema keys the row on `environment_id` and sets `credentials_ref` as a reference into `service-secrets`, while the Tier paragraph keeps the vault enterprise and the row per organization. Where the open tier's supplied token is kept at rest is therefore unstated; add it to "Step 2 owes" (ADR-0143 and ADR-0100 give the open connector credential path).

N2 (nit) — ADR-0030's two amended passages say "managed credentials" and drop "the vault"; the item-3 text also drops "self-hosted". Both point at the addendum, which is complete.

N3 (nit) — rider 1 of `7024100939` notes §8 requires an audit row on link creation. The addendum replaces §8 item 2, the only place that row was required; say that a confirmed link keeps its audit row.

No must-fix. The binding rule is "email match proposes, person confirms once" as ruled, the open tier is not widened in ADR-0013, the scope is DMs only, and all five unbind riders are present.
